clue.text: Verse, one read by short eccentric clergyman

indicators.note: something read by a person sits right beside them, so one piece is placed alongside the next
a word made short loses its final letter before use

blocks.note: V is the standard abbreviation for verse
the Roman numeral for one
a card is an odd, amusing person

explanation.surface: A quirky little cleric is handed a verse to read aloud in church.
explanation.walkthrough: A card is an old-fashioned word for an eccentric character; shortened it loses its D, giving VI + CAR = VICAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a Church of England priest in charge of a parish, so a type of clergyman.

clue.text: Leave Virginia to provide food? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of the phrase before it is dropped

blocks.note: the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
to cater is to supply food for an event

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to leave Virginia, perhaps to take up catering elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: CATER loses its final R, and VA + CATE gives VACATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacate a room or post is to go out of it, so it is a synonym of the verb leave.

clue.text: Architectural eyesore in stone

blocks.note: first meaning: an ugly building spoiling its surroundings
second meaning: a red gemstone, especially a garnet cut en cabochon

explanation.surface: An ugly building has been put up in stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Charles famously called a proposed National Gallery extension a 'monstrous carbuncle', fixing the first sense in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a red garnet gem and, figuratively, an unsightly modern building blighting its setting.

clue.text: Farm operated with support of church

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so the second piece follows below the first

blocks.note: past tense of run, as in running a machine
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A farm run with backing from the local church.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large livestock farm, especially in North America, so a kind of farm.

clue.text: Playboy's black gun dog

blocks.note: jet is a black stone, and jet-black means deep black
a setter is a breed of dog used in shooting

explanation.surface: A wealthy playboy's dark gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet-setter is a wealthy pleasure-seeker who flies between fashionable resorts, much like a playboy.

clue.text: Handyman in lift, roasted dreadfully about sink

indicators.note: something done dreadfully is badly mangled, so those letters are scrambled
about means going round, so the scrambled letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: to jack up is to lift, and a jack is a lifting device
anagram fodder
to sink is to fall

explanation.surface: A handyman stuck in a lift, badly roasted, near a sink.
explanation.walkthrough: Lift looks like a place the handyman is trapped, but it is a verb; the anagram is split by the inserted piece rather than kept whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack of all trades can turn a hand to many jobs, which is what a handyman does.

clue.text: Where teachers were in a class of their own?

definitions.text: Where teachers were in a class of their own?

blocks.clueFragment: in a class of their own
blocks.note: surface reading: teachers who were outstanding, beyond compare
setter's reading: the place trainee teachers sat as students in their own class

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'in a class of their own' means peerless, but here it is literal: student teachers formed a class at the institution that trained them.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachers used to qualify at a specialist college for trainees, where they sat in classes made up of fellow future teachers.

clue.text: Divert to harbour

blocks.note: first meaning: to amuse
second meaning: to hold in mind, as with a hope or doubt

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests rerouting a ship into port; both words are verbs with figurative senses.
explanation.definitionFit: One may entertain guests by amusing them, and entertain a notion by keeping it in mind, as one harbours a grudge.

clue.text: Volunteers to house a member from Florida resort

indicators.note: to house something is to give it a home inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
taken as written
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Volunteers put up a politician who has come from a Florida resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA, or Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a city on the Gulf coast of Florida, popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Girl, Flower Queen in May

indicators.note: in places the royal letter inside the name of the month

blocks.note: the rose is a flower
taken as written
R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A girl crowned as the flower queen at a May festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower Queen in May' suggests a May Queen, but Queen is just the royal R, and May is the month taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is a female given name, so it can stand for a girl, a common crossword convention.

clue.text: Very serious, the Parisian being deleted from register

indicators.note: being deleted from says the following word loses the stated part

blocks.note: le is French for the
a chronicle is a record of events

explanation.surface: A grave matter: a Parisian has been struck off the register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Parisian' means the word 'the' in French, LE, which is removed from the end of CHRONICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronic is used colloquially in Britain for something very bad, and medically for a persistent, serious condition.

clue.text: Master misguided about one Greek goddess

indicators.note: misguided means led astray, so those letters wander out of order
about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the numeral

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A misled master turns to a single Greek goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis is the Greek goddess of hunting and the moon, counterpart of the Roman Diana.

clue.text: Move southward to develop land

blocks.note: to move someone emotionally is to touch them
southward is down on a map

explanation.surface: Heading south to build on a plot of land.
explanation.walkthrough: Land looks like a noun meaning real estate, but it is the verb used of aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: When an aircraft lands it makes touchdown on the runway, so the two express the same arrival.

clue.text: Area in actual miles

blocks.note: real means actual, genuine
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: Measuring an area in true miles.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a field or domain, as in the realm of science, so it means area.

clue.text: Preliminary event Austrian crier broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, like seed, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An Austrian town crier is heard on the radio before the main event.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain-raiser was a short play before the main piece, now any warm-up or opening event.

clue.text: Give back control, say

blocks.note: to rein something in is to control it
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A call to hand back power to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give back control' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Give back'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone to a former post or something to former use, so to give it back.

clue.text: Firm dates broken in rapid succession

indicators.note: something broken falls to pieces, and the pieces are reassembled in another order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
things happening fast come one after another quickly

explanation.surface: Fixed appointments are being cancelled one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast describes someone resolute and unwavering, and firm in the same sense of not budging.

clue.text: Blow up and erupt, possibly enveloping country's capital

indicators.note: possibly signals that the word is one possible arrangement of letters, not the only one
a capital is a head letter, so the word's opening letter is taken
enveloping means wrapping round, so the rearranged letters surround the selected one

blocks.note: taken as written
anagram fodder
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A volcano blows up and erupts across a nation's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Country's capital suggests a city such as Paris, but it means only the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is an upward punch in boxing, a kind of blow delivered to the chin.

clue.text: A taking of liberties? Concept I lie about to church

indicators.note: about can mean in a disordered way, here turning the letters round
to here means added on, so the next abbreviation is joined at the end

blocks.note: anagram fodder
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone admits lying about a church-related idea, a liberty taken with the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic licence is a writer's freedom to depart from facts or rules for effect, so it is a liberty taken.

clue.text: Light-hearted bishop, flexible

blocks.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
lithe means supple, flexible

explanation.surface: A cheerful, supple bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe describes someone happy and carefree, with no weight on their spirits.

clue.text: The Spanish left island, US island

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
L is the abbreviation for left
IS is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Spaniards departing one island for another in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Spanish left' looks like Spaniards departing, but it is three separate parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellis Island in New York Harbor was the main immigration station into the United States.

clue.text: Christmas coming up? Get in a bit of mixed fruit

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the word reads from bottom to top
a bit of a word is just one letter, here its first
get in tells the selected letter to go inside the turned word

blocks.note: Noel is another word for Christmas
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Christmas approaches, so buy some mixed fruit for the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon is a sour yellow citrus fruit.

clue.text: After spin, reportedly pilot's a good example to follow

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is heard, so the word is spelt by its sound
after puts the second piece following the first

blocks.note: a roll is a spinning movement, as of a plane
a pilot version is a trial model

explanation.surface: An aerobatic pilot rolling in the air sets a fine example.
explanation.walkthrough: Pilot suggests an aviator, which suits spin; here it is the adjective-like trial sense, as in a pilot scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is someone whose behaviour others copy, a person worth imitating.

clue.text: Copper, and others, after leader of Mafia?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
et al is the Latin abbreviation for and others

explanation.surface: A police officer and colleagues chase the boss of the Mafia.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman tailing the Mafia, but here it is the element; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is one example of a metal, a reddish conductive element, so the definition names one member of a class.

clue.text: Order Green Beret to fire round

indicators.note: to fire is to dismiss, so the named letter is thrown out

blocks.note: the Green Berets are British Royal Marine commandos
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A soldier is ordered to fire a round.
explanation.walkthrough: Fire looks like shooting, which suits a soldier and a round, but it means sack: the O-shaped letter is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an instruction from a superior that must be obeyed, as in a military directive.

clue.text: Clipping from special edition shown to court

indicators.note: shown to joins one piece directly onto the next

blocks.note: an extra is a special edition of a newspaper
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A newspaper cutting from a special edition is produced as evidence in court.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a short passage taken from a longer text, like a clipping cut from a newspaper.

clue.text: Williams, say, showing extraordinary net sense at end of game

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged
the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tennis player called Williams shows remarkable sense at the net to close out the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Williams suggests the tennis sisters, backed by net and game, but it means the playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee Williams was the American playwright of A Streetcar Named Desire, so the name is a forename shared, by example.

clue.text: Machine responsible for state of agitation, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to be in a lather is to be worked up

explanation.surface: A machine that has been causing everyone a lot of stress.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a workshop tool that spins wood or metal for shaping, so it is a machine.
